newsitem.title: USA: Court strikes down Wisconsin school choice plan.
newsitem.headline: Court strikes down Wisconsin school choice plan.

text.p: A court Wednesday ruled as unconstitutional a plan to provide state money for tuition to send children to church-based private schools.
The ruling in Dane County Circuit Court will be appealed, Edward Marion, a lawyer for Gov. Tommy Thompson told Reuters.

Thompson had made the tuition plan a centrepiece of his educational reform efforts. As originally passed in 1990 the plan did not allow state money to be paid for tuition to sectarian schools, but that was amended by the state legislature.
Marion said Wednesday's ruling essentially gutted the programme, however, since there were very few private schools that were not church-based.
"Without them there aren't enough schools to educate the children involved," he said. "It could have been expanded to 15,000 children in Milwaukee compared to only about 1,600 now," he said.
Last spring the Wisconsin Supreme Court deadlocked on the issue and sent it back to the trial court for a decision, which was announced Wednesday.
